title: LP Team
field: linear programming solver engineering, centred on the revised simplex method and above all the dual revised simplex method (pricing and CHUZR, bound-flipping ratio tests, dual steepest edge, sparse LU factorization and its updates, hyper-sparsity, parallel simplex), together with the primal simplex, start bases and crash, sifting, and the measurement of production LP codes on real models, as built into research and production LP solvers; the MIP work of two members (John J. H. Forrest: Cbc and earlier MIP codes; Robert E. Bixby: CPLEX and Gurobi MIP progress measurement) is seated in the MILP Team (product/milp-team, where they sit as guests from lp-team) and is not this team's centre; interior-point / barrier, first-order (PDLP-type) LP, crossover and presolve are not the centre of any member's work
chase_hints: Optimization Online (optimization-online.org)
arXiv math.OC
University of Edinburgh: ERGO technical reports on Julian Hall's pages (webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/hall/) and the Edinburgh Research Archive (era.ed.ac.uk)
solver documentation and open source (HiGHS: github.com/ERGO-Code/HiGHS, ergo-code.github.io/HiGHS; COPT: guide.coap.online/copt/en-doc/; COIN-OR Clp; FICO Xpress manuals)
Hans Mittelmann's benchmark pages (plato.asu.edu/bench.html) for solver context only, never as the member's own words

card_dimensions.D3: problem class and data model: the LP form handled (bounded variables, computational form, slack basis), the sparsity / structure / scale properties of the instances that the technique relies on or exploits (hyper-sparsity, density, block structure), and the assumptions stated for any correctness argument
card_dimensions.D4: algorithm and implementation design: data structures and linear-algebra kernels (sparse LU factorization, FTRAN / BTRAN, basis-update schemes), pivoting and pricing rules (CHUZR, CHUZC, dual steepest edge), numerical safeguards (tolerances, Harris and bound-flipping ratio tests, perturbation), task decomposition for parallelism, and any proof or invariant together with the device used
card_dimensions.D5: computational evaluation: test set, baselines (named solvers and versions), metrics (iterations, time, geometric-mean speed-up, performance profiles), hardware and thread counts, and whether failures or slowdowns are reported

members.name: John J. H. Forrest
members.hint: Simplex-code author: wrote COIN-OR Clp (primal and dual simplex, first commit 2002-07-30), Abc/Aboca (parallel dual, 2012) and CoinUtils' CoinFactorization; Forrest-Tomlin basis update (Math. Programming 1972), Forrest-Goldfarb steepest edge (Math. Programming 1992), Sprint (sifting) and the Idiot crash; earlier Scicon Ltd (UMPIRE 1974) and IBM Research (YKTLP/OSL with J. A. Tomlin; retired, date unknown, between 2006 and 2010); founding 'Benevolent Dictator' of COIN-OR. CODE-FIRST LENS, on the pattern of andreas-wachter (product/nonlinear-team: Ipopt code plus 681 mailing-list answers) and michael-powell (product/dfo-team: Fortran code and cover notes): his papers are few and all co-authored, so the primary evidence is the Clp, Abc, CoinUtils and Cbc source, the first-person design notes in it, the commit history, his 461 GitHub issue and PR comments (2017-11-20 to 2026-11-01; most are on Cbc) and the 1998 Anbil-Forrest-Pulleyblank ICM chapter. SCOPE: LP simplex engineering AND, added 2026-11-05 because the user also seats him in the MILP Team, his MIP craft: Cbc (COIN-OR branch and cut) and the earlier MIP codes (UMPIRE with Hirst and Tomlin; OSL's MIP); the MIP items in chase_hints are leads to verify with tools, not facts. AUTHORSHIP LABELS THAT MUST SURVIVE INTO THE SKILL: his code authorship covers Clp, Abc and CoinFactorization; Cbc is code evidence too, shared with others: its README (read 2026-11-05) says 'Cbc is developed by John Forrest, now retired from IBM Research, and others', and the 2005 COIN-OR INFORMS Cup page calls him author of CLP and CBC, but a given Cbc part is his only where its Authors lines or history show it (Cbc has other major committers (GitHub contributors count on 2026-11-05: h-g-s 807 against johnjforrest 797 and jjhforrest 263; Ted Ralphs and others); check Authors lines and history before calling a Cbc part his); Cgl (the cut generators Cbc calls) is shared code as well: a generator counts as his only where the Cgl AUTHORS file (read 2026-11-05) names him 'contributor' (it does for CglAllDifferent, CglCutGenerator, CglDuplicateRow, CglGomory, CglMessage, CglMixedIntegerRounding2, CglOddHole, CglPreProcess, CglProbing and CglStored), and counts as his practice only as far as its history shows (the T1 notes trace CglPreProcess and most of CglProbing to him); a bare name or 'PM' alone in that file (e.g. CglGMI, CglRedSplit2, CglKnapsackCover, CglFlowCover) is not authorship; YKTLP, OSL (including its MIP, unless code or his own statement shows otherwise), LAMPS and UMPIRE are credit by others or co-authored papers (no code of his visible; the OSL factorization in CoinUtils is a 2009 port of IBM code, and its first-person lines read as a porter's); not all of Clp is his (ClpPdco: Tomlin; ClpPE*: Omer and Towhidi; some presolve comments read as other hands). The GitHub accounts johnjforrest (2002-2020, fastercoin.com email) and jjhforrest (2020-) are linked to him by strong inference (same display name, hand-over 2020-05-11/12, JJHF-signed comments), not by any document. 'living' rests on that account activity (latest 2026-11-01). OpenAlex: pin author A5061258306 (a name search returns other people). Name forms: John J. Forrest, J. J. H. Forrest, John Forrest; not Jeffrey Yi-Lin Forrest or other Forrests. ROUNDTABLE CARD (added 2026-11-05 at the user's request): one card serves two teams. The LP Team reads it here, and the MILP Team (product/milp-team) seats this member as a guest and reads this same card from product/lp-team/john-j-h-forrest/SKILL.md. So its 'Leads when' bullet must say, in two labelled parts, when the lens leads on LP and when it leads on MIP, each part resting on the methods that hold in that domain; where the MIP evidence is thin, the card says so instead of padding it.

members.name: Robert E. Bixby
members.hint: Rice University mathematician who wrote the original CPLEX simplex code and co-founded CPLEX Optimization (1987/88) and later Gurobi (2008; CEO until 3 September 2015). SCOPE OF THIS LENS: DECISION AND MEASUREMENT CRAFT FOR LP AND MIP, in two parts. (1) LP, 1987-2002: what to build next in a production simplex code, how to measure it on real customer models, how to read version-to-version and algorithm-to-algorithm comparisons, from these primary sources: 'Solving Real-World Linear Programs: A Decade and More of Progress', Operations Research 50(1):3-15, 2002 (DOI 10.1287/opre.50.1.3.17780); 'A Brief History of Linear and Mixed-Integer Programming Computation', Documenta Math. Extra Vol. ISMP 2012, 107-121; the Optima 101 interview (questions October 2015, issue September 2016); ZIB SC 92-11 'Das Implementieren des Simplex-Verfahrens: Die Startbasis' (German, April 1992; English version ORSA J. Comput. 4(3):267-284, 1992); ZIB SC-95-45, Bixby and Martin, 'Parallelizing the Dual Simplex Method' (December 1995 preprint; published INFORMS J. Comput. 12(1):45-56, 2000); and the September 2022 Hausdorff School deck 'Linear Programming: A Historical View'. Of his other LP works only the LP subset counts (initial basis, the 1992 interior-point and simplex case study with sifting, the 1994 commentary 'Progress in Linear Programming', basis recovery from an interior point, embedded network rows). (2) MIP, added 2026-11-05 because the user also seats him in the MILP Team: CPLEX and Gurobi MIP and the MIP progress measurements in his papers and talks, including the MIP parts of the Documenta 2012 paper and of the Hausdorff 2022 deck; the MIP items in chase_hints are leads to verify with tools, not facts. Matroid and TSP work are context only, unless the research shows they matter for the LP or MIP craft (TSP/Concorde is joint work with Applegate, Chvatal and Cook, roles not divided). AUTHORSHIP LABELS THAT MUST SURVIVE INTO THE SKILL: LP: his authorship stops at his own statements: the main parts of the CPLEX simplex as of April 1992 (SC 92-11, printed p. 2), all development at the 1988 first release (Optima 101 p. 3), still doing development in 1997 (Optima 101 p. 4), and no development at Gurobi (Optima 101 pp. 4-5). Later CPLEX changes (5.0 to 7.1 and after) are not shown to be his: OR 2002 p. 14 credits Gu, Lustig, Rothberg and Wunderling with fundamental contributions to the LP algorithms. Dual steepest edge is Forrest and Goldfarb's method that CPLEX implemented, by his own texts. MIP: authorship and role labels rest on his own dated statements, as for LP; lead to verify in Optima 101 pp. 3-5: by his own account MIP cuts and most presolve were Gu's, node presolve, probing and parallel barrier Rothberg's, early MIP codes such as MINTO beat CPLEX, and he put strong branching into CPLEX after a discussion with Cook; with no development at Gurobi, his MIP lens is measurement and decision craft, not MIP code, and a progress number measured on a code is not evidence that he wrote what produced it. LIVING STATUS AND PRESENT ROLE ARE NOT ESTABLISHED by any dated source. The latest dated trace found is the long-form 'Subject to: Robert Bixby' interview on YouTube, uploaded 2023-12-06 Pacific time (2023-12-07 UTC; page metadata read 2026-11-05; recording date not stated), later than the September 2022 Hausdorff deck; the T1 research also found a 29 September 2024 NAE programme that lists his name (a listing only); Rothberg became Gurobi chairman on 2 January 2023. The 'living' key is deliberately left out of this entry until the user decides; the skill must not state either. OpenAlex author A5012463224 (one MIP paper sits under a split record, A5097662446). The LP Team reads it here, and the MILP Team (product/milp-team) seats this member as a guest and reads this same card from product/lp-team/robert-e-bixby/SKILL.md. So its 'Leads when' bullet must say, in two labelled parts, when the lens leads on LP and when it leads on MIP, each part resting on the methods that hold in that domain; where the MIP evidence is thin, the card says so instead of padding it.
